Since "not working" can mean several different things (e.g., it won't start, it runs but doesn't heat, or it makes a weird noise), I will cover the most common causes and troubleshooting steps.

### 🔍 First: Identify the Symptom
• Won’t turn on at all? → Check power/lint filter/door switch.
• Turns on but doesn’t dry clothes? → Likely airflow or heating issue.
• Turns on, heats up, then shuts off? → Overheating (vent blockage).
• Making loud noises? → Drum rollers or belt issue.

---

## ✅ Step-by-Step Troubleshooting Guide

### 1. Check the Power Source
• Electric Dryers: Ensure the plug is firmly in the outlet. Test another device in the same outlet to confirm power. If it’s a 240V circuit (common for electric dryers), check your home’s breaker panel for a tripped breaker or blown fuse.
• Gas Dryers: Ensure the gas supply valve is open. Check if other gas appliances are working.

### 2. Clean the Lint Filter
• A clogged lint filter restricts airflow, causing poor drying and overheating (which can shut the dryer off).
• Remove the filter, clean it thoroughly with a brush or vacuum, and reinsert it properly.

### 3. Inspect the Vent/Hose (Most Common Cause of Poor Drying)
• Blocked Vents: Disconnect the vent hose from the back of the dryer and check for lint buildup. Also check the exterior vent hood outside your home to ensure the flap opens freely and isn’t blocked by lint, bird nests, or debris.
• Crushed Hose: Ensure the flexible or rigid vent hose behind the dryer isn’t kinked or crushed.

### 4. Check the Door Switch
• If the dryer won’t start when you press “Start,” the door switch may be faulty. The dryer should not run if it thinks the door is open.
• Test: Close the door firmly and listen for a click. If no click, or if it still doesn’t start, the switch may need replacement.

### 5. For Gas Dryers: Check the Igniter & Flame Sensor
• If the dryer tumbles but produces no heat, the igniter may be broken (it should glow orange) or the flame sensor may be dirty/faulty.
• Note: If you smell gas at any point, turn off the gas supply immediately and call a professional.

### 6. For Electric Dryers: Check the Heating Element & Thermal Fuse
• Heating Element: If visible (behind the front or rear panel), check for breaks in the coil.
• Thermal Fuse: This safety device blows if the dryer overheats (often due to a clogged vent). It’s usually located on the dryer’s exhaust housing. Use a multimeter to test for continuity.

### 7. Check the Drum Belts and Rollers
• If the drum doesn’t turn, the belt may be broken or slipped off.
• If it makes a loud thumping or squealing noise, the drum rollers or glides may be worn out.

---

## 🛠️ When to Call a Professional
Call a qualified technician if:
• You’re uncomfortable opening panels or testing electrical components.
• The issue involves gas lines, gas valves, or complex electronic control boards.
• Basic troubleshooting (cleaning lint/vents) doesn’t resolve the problem.
• You suspect a motor failure or major internal component damage.

---

## 💡 Prevention Tips
1. Clean the lint filter after every load.
2. Vacuum the vent hose and exterior vent hood at least once a year.
3. Don’t overload the dryer – clothes need space to tumble for proper drying.
4. Ensure the dryer has adequate clearance from walls and cabinets for airflow.

If you can provide more details (e.g., “It runs but no heat” or “It won’t start”), I can give you more specific advice!
It's a Hotpoint condenser dryer. Lights come on but nothing happens when I press start, no sound at all. Started this morning.

Since it is a Hotpoint Condenser Dryer and there are lights but zero sound/no movement, the issue is likely electrical or related to a safety interlock rather than a mechanical failure (like a broken belt).

Here are the most common causes for this specific symptom, ranked from easiest to fix to more complex:

### 1. Check the Door Switch (Most Likely)
Condenser dryers have a safety switch that prevents the motor from running if the door isn’t fully closed or latched. If this switch fails or gets stuck, the dryer will show lights but refuse to start.
• Test: Open and close the door firmly several times. Listen/feel for a distinct "click" inside the door frame when it closes.
• Check: Look at the latch on the door and the corresponding striker plate on the body. Is anything broken, loose, or obstructed by lint/clothes?

### 2. Check the Moisture Sensor / Drum Rotation
Some Hotpoint models have a safety feature that prevents starting if the drum is manually rotated in the wrong direction (though rare) or if the moisture sensors are shorting out.
• Test: Try turning the drum by hand gently. If it feels completely seized, there may be an obstruction under the drum (e.g., a lost sock, coin, or bra wire stuck between the inner and outer drums). This can jam the motor so hard that the start circuit doesn’t engage.

### 3. Check the Thermal Fuse / Overheat Thermostat
If the dryer overheated recently (even if you didn’t notice), the thermal fuse may have blown as a safety measure. This cuts power to the motor and control board, but often leaves the display lights on because they are powered separately or via a different circuit.
• Location: Usually located at the back of the dryer near the heater housing or inside the drum casing.
• Test: You will need to unplug the dryer, remove the top or rear panel (depending on model), and use a multimeter to check for continuity across the thermal fuse. If it has no continuity, replace it.

### 4. Check the Start Switch / Control Panel
The physical "Start" button itself may have failed internally. Since there’s no sound at all, the control board isn’t receiving the signal to engage the motor relay.
• Test: Press the start button firmly and listen closely near the control panel for any faint click from a relay. If you hear nothing, the switch or the main control PCB may be faulty.

### 5. Check the Motor Capacitor (If Applicable)
Some Hotpoint condenser models use a capacitor to help start the motor. If this fails, the dryer might hum but not turn. However, since you said no sound at all, this is less likely unless the entire control circuit is dead.

---

### 🛠️ Recommended Next Steps:
1.  Unplug the dryer for 5–10 minutes to reset the electronic control board. Plug it back in and try again.
2.  Inspect the door latch thoroughly. Clean any lint from around the switch mechanism.
3.  Check for obstructions by feeling inside the drum (with power off) for anything stuck between the drums.
4.  If none of these work, the issue is likely a failed door switch, blown thermal fuse, or faulty control board. These require disassembly and potentially part replacement.

If you’re not comfortable opening the appliance, I recommend contacting a qualified technician, especially since condenser dryers involve electrical components near water/moisture systems.
No click when the door shuts, it swings back slightly open. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, I found the piece on the floor.

That explains everything! The "click" you were expecting is the door interlock switch. Because the plastic latch (tongue) broke, the door isn't pushing the switch in when it closes. The dryer’s safety system sees the door as open and refuses to start the motor or any other functions, which is why there are lights but no movement or sound.

### 🛠️ How to Fix It

You have two main options: Temporary Fix (to get it running today) and Permanent Repair.

#### ✅ Option 1: Temporary "Bypass" (Do this at your own risk)
⚠️ Warning: This disables a safety feature. Only do this if you are comfortable working with electrical components and will ensure the door stays closed manually during operation. Never leave the dryer unattended while using this method.

1.  Unplug the dryer from the mains power first.
2.  Locate the door interlock switch. It’s usually behind the front panel or near the top of the door frame, where the plastic latch would normally hit it. You may need to remove a few screws from the top or front panel to access it.
3.  Identify the two wires connected to the common terminal of the switch (usually the ones that complete the circuit when the door is closed).
4.  Carefully disconnect these two wires and twist them together securely with a wire nut or electrical tape. This "jumps" the circuit, telling the dryer the door is closed.
5.  Reassemble the panels, plug the dryer back in, and close the door firmly (you may need to hold it shut or prop it with a wedge if it swings open). Press start.

#### ✅ Option 2: Permanent Repair (Recommended)
You need to replace the door latch assembly or the entire front panel/door hinge assembly, depending on your specific Hotpoint model.

1.  Find Your Model Number: Look for a sticker inside the door frame, on the top edge of the dryer, or on the back. It usually starts with something like `TDC...` or `WMT...`.
2.  Order the Part: Search online retailers (like Amazon, eBay, or appliance parts sites) using your model number + "door latch" or "door interlock."
3.  Replace It:
    • Unplug the dryer.
    • Remove the top and/or front panels (usually held by screws behind the lint filter or under a clip).
    • Unscrew the broken plastic latch from the door or frame.
    • Install the new one, reconnect any wires if they were attached to the latch itself (some are part of the switch housing), and reassemble.

### 💡 Pro Tip for Next Time
When loading clothes, make sure nothing is caught in the door seal or between the drum opening and the glass. This is often what causes these plastic latches to snap under pressure.

Let me know your model number if you’d like help finding the exact part!
